thread:
incident-bot: Paging: multiple container restarts on dedicated-gpu-1 cluster during prefill phase — observed GPU OOM / CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS. Severity: P1. @oncall @sre.

alice: Ack. I'm oncall. Seeing increased 5xxs from the inference gateway. Route /v1/generate returning 503s intermittently. Can someone grab logs from the node pool?

samir: grabbing logs now. Quick paste of journalctl and container logs:

```
[2026-03-15T02:10:12Z] runtime: prefill task started, seq_len=120234 tokens, model="rwkv-30b-v2"
[2026-03-15T02:10:12Z] runtime: allocating kv cache bytes=24576000000 (~24.6GB)
[2026-03-15T02:10:13Z] CUDA: out of memory when allocating 24576000000 bytes
[2026-03-15T02:10:13Z] runtime: container restart requested (OOM)
[2026-03-15T02:10:14Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (GPU 0): 79, a bunch of GPU memory errors
```

samir: Looks like long-context prefill for a customer session blew past our kv cache guardrails and pushed the GPU to OOM, causing the runtime to crash and k8s to restart the pod. Multiple pods in the same node pool hit this pattern within 2 minutes.

lena: Confirmed. Network telemetry shows burst of very large prompts from a few client API keys. Initial impact: ~5% error rate across that region for ~7 minutes. We should throttle/blackhole those keys and enable fallback routing.

eric: Which customers affected? Support put a hold on inbound. I have two customer IDs from logs: cust_51 and cust_98. Both reported slow responses, one retried and succeeded later.

oncall-junior: Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) Add an immediate runtime guard to reject prefill requests with seq_len > 65k tokens with a 400 + reason. 2) Route suspected heavy sessions to cpu-fallback or a low-memory model variant. 3) Cordon the affected node to stop further restarts while we hotfix.

alice: Agreed. Samir, can you push a temporary guard into the runtime config (env MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS=65536) and restart the runtime on the affected pool only? We want minimal blast radius.

samir: Applying config change to deployment dedicated-gpu-1/runtime via k8s patch now. Command I ran: 

```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runtime MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS=65536 --record
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime -n inference --selector=pool=dedicated-gpu-1
```

samir: Rolling restart issued. Monitoring pod restarts...

incident-bot: Deploy event: set env MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS=65536 on deployment/runtime (pool=dedicated-gpu-1). Rollout started.

lena: I'm also throttling the API keys via the gateway for suspicious keys (cust_51, cust_98). Rate limit set to 1 rps for those keys and 50% of new requests are routed to cpu-fallback.

eric: Customer-facing: support DM to cust_51 and cust_98 acknowledging degraded responses and retry recommendation. No data loss. ETA for fix: ~15-20m.

oncall-junior: While the restart is happening, I drained the worst-performing node: `kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. The node had 6 OOM-restarted pods in the last 5 min.

samir: Rollout finished on 4/4 pods in pool. New pods boot with MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS=65536. Initial telemetry shows prefill requests >65k tokens are now rejected at the runtime edge. Error rate dropping.

sre-robot: Alert suppressed: multiple OOM spikes suppressed for 30m based on recent mitigations.

alice: Good. Next steps: - Short-term: keep MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS env for 24h, keep customer throttles for 1h, monitor. - Medium: add runtime defensive prefill allocator that attempts incremental KV allocation and falls back to CPU if GPU allocation fails, plus explicit per-key quota for max seq_len. - Long-term: add token-counting client-side guard in SDKs and a model admission policy enforced at the gateway.

eric: I'll prepare a customer-impact note for the postmortem thread and notify the two customers.

oncall-junior: For the post-incident action item: add a k8s pod-level OOM backoff policy so a single malicious/abusive prefill can't cause repeated node pressure.

samir: Filed hotfix change PR for runtime: add MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS reject + incremental kv allocator prototype. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

alice: Thanks everyone. We'll keep this thread open for the postmortem. If error rates stay low for 30m, I'll move to monitoring-only.

incident-bot: Incident P1 update: reduced impact, mitigations applied. Next update in 30m or on status change. :white_check_mark:
